minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 21, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:07 p.m., on April 21, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 16, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:28 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness (arrived at 6:00 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:08 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:03
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

City Council Minutes  1  April 21, 2014
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim April 26, 2014, to be "Earth Day and Arbor Day"

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill
  and Environmental Program Administrator Denise Matson.

P2. Featured Business of the Month - The Shirt Cannery

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Julie Marshall, owner of the Shirt Cannery.

RECESS

Due to audio-visual technical issues, Mayor Kelley declared a recess at 6:17 p.m. The City
Council reconvened at 6:38 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

P3. School Spotlight - Reilly Elementary

  The City Council received the presentation from Principal Jill Brennan.

P4. School Spotlight - Trabuco Hills High School

  The City Council received the presentation from Justin LaSor, a Junior student at Trabuco
  Hills High School.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Desi Joseph Kiss, M.V.: proposed that the subject of adding restrooms to city parks be placed on
the November ballot and he presented his own plan to install 20 new restrooms for a price not to
exceed $2 million.

Dan Avery, M.V.: on behalf of his dog, he thanked the City for the new La Paws Dog Park.

Jim Carlin, M.V.: referring to agenda item 28, he recommended that the City Council not rename
the Mission Viejo Library.

Matt Corrigan, M.V.: discussed his opposition to taxpayers footing the bill for facility upgrades
and he stated that those who enjoy tennis or a dog park should do so with their own time and
money.

Stephanie Tanton, M.V.: invited the community to the upcoming Arts Alive event on May 3 and
4, 2014, at the Norman P. Murray Community Center and Village Green.

City Council Minutes  2  April 21, 2014
 Joe Tully, M.V.: stated that sports field demands are at the same level as they were in 2006 and
he expressed his support for the installation of restrooms in neighborhood parks.

Julie Tully, M.V.: referencing the recent Community Services Commission meeting, she stated
that she felt some of the Commissioners had already made up their mind on the park restroom
matter and she reminded the Council that the restrooms were deemed necessary 8 years ago.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 9, 11, 13, and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 7, 2014, as presented.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2014

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2014

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2014

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  April 21, 2014
 8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for February 2014

  Received and filed.

10. Los Alisos Boulevard Pavement Rehabilitation, Interstate 5 to Santa Margarita
  Parkway (CIP 837)

  Approved the bid specifications and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for
  the subject project.

12. Purchase of Four Replacement Bi-Fuel, Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Fleet Trucks

  Awarded purchase agreement for four (4) Bi-Fuel, CNG Fleet Trucks to Wondries Fleet
  Group in an amount not to exceed $197,670.68.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Schlicht

28. William S. Craycraft Learning and Technology Center

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  The following spoke in opposition to the renaming of the library: Dan Avery, M.V.;
  Elizabeth Busick, M.V.; Lenore Powell, M.V.; Beth McConaughy, M.V.; Dick
  McConaughy, M.V.; Hugh Armstrong, M.V.; Jim Carlin, M.V.; Randy Smith, M.V.; and
  Liz Duran-Smetana, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of renaming the library: Chuck Costello, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  direct the Community Services Commission to evaluate options for naming a facility or
  event after Bill Craycraft (along with the City Council suggestions) and return to the
  Council with recommendations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  4  April 21, 2014
 29. Progress Report on the Contract Negotiations with the Nadadores

  Council Member Schlicht presented her agenda report.

  Matt Corrigan, M.V.: noted that the facility that the Nadadores use is not open to the public
  and it is not fair to ask residents to pay for private facilities.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is concerned about spending taxpayer dollars on a
  private facility and she would like for the City to hold a workshop for public input.

  This matter was set aside while the Council addressed agenda item 18.

NEW BUSINESS

18. Mission Viejo Nadadores Facilities Use Agreement

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and outlined highlights of the proposed agreement.

  The following spoke in support of the proposed Nadadores Facilities Use Agreement: Brian
  Goodell, M.V.; Wendy Bucknum, M.V.; Beverly Montrella, M.V.; and Judy Bullockus,
  M.V.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed agreement: Matt Corrigan, M.V. and
  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) approve the
  agreement (A14-09) to form and content and authorize the City Manager to make any
  minor final changes to the agreement and to have the Mayor sign the final agreement, and
  (2) reject the recommendation for agenda item 29.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 9:28 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:36
p.m. with three City Council Members present. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness and Council Member
Reardon returned at 9:37 p.m.

City Council Minutes  5  April 21, 2014
 OLD BUSINESS

15. Montanoso Locker Room Rehabilitation and Expansion (CIP 500)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  approve the bid specifications and plans, and authorize staff to advertise for bids for the
  Montanoso Locker Room Rehabilitation Expansion; (2) award a contract to Friess
  Company Builders, Inc.,(A14-05) in the amount not to exceed $40,300 for construction
  management and observation, and issue a purchase order; (3) award a contract to Robert R.
  Coffee Architects + Associates (A14-06) in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00 for
  Construction submittal review and observation, and issue a purchase order; and (4) issue a
  purchase order to Petra Geotechnical Consultants in an amount not to exceed $4,220.00 for
  soil testing, compaction testing during construction.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16. Pavion Park (CIP 303)

  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, presented the staff
  report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to remove
  the shade element over the large climbing structure and award a contract in an amount not
  to exceed $888,774.00 to Hondo Company Inc. (A14-07) and issue a purchase order, and
  (2) award a contract to Gametime c/o Great Western (A14-08) in an amount not to exceed
  $260,258.91 and issue a purchase order.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

17. Mission Viejo Dog Park Completion (CIP 313)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  6  April 21, 2014
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  certify the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorize
  the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to record
  the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty-five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; (4) authorize the payment of the final retention of $53,371.49, thirty-
  five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion; and (5) authorize
  staff to spend the balance of the project funds on the providing additional site elements at
  the Dog Park.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register dated March 28, 2014, in the amount of $899,491.89

  Council Member Schlicht asked about the purchase of animal traps.

  Director Rattay responded that the Animal Services Officers uses traps to capture small
  animals as necessary.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment for dog park donations.

  Mr. Rattay responded that the IT department purchased software that would allow the City
  to take financial donations online.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register dated April 4, 2014, in the amount of $762,949.91

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about a payment to Getty Images and asked why the
  City doesn't use free Google images.

City Council Minutes  7  April 21, 2014
   Karen Hamman, City Clerk/Director of Community Relations, responded that the City
  cannot use images taken from the Internet as there are copyright infringement issues.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment to Nichols Consulting Engineering.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon confirmed that the payment was for a Pavement
  Management Report and the report is still being put together but it will be available to the
  public when complete.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2014-2015 Detailing City’s Proposed
  Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the Community Services Commission passed this with
  a 5-2 vote and there were some concerns about providing funds to illegal aliens, the scoring
  system and confusion with the application. She stated that Mission Viejo residents were
  given a low score and there seemed to be some unfairness in the process.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Consultant Mike Linares discussed
  the concerns that were cited. Elaine Lister noted that while there was some confusion with
  one of the questions that came to light at the Community Services Commission meeting,
  staff later called the applicants and confirmed both their understanding of the question and
  their response. Consequently staff feels confident with the funding recommendation, as did
  the Planning and Transportation Commission when they reviewed the item. Mr. Linares
  added that the evaluation criteria used for scoring the applications was reviewed and
  approved by a prior City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to adopt
  Resolution 14-12 Approving the City's Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY)
  2014-2015 Detailing City's Proposed Use of Community Development Block Grant
  (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of Such Plans to the U.S. Department of
  Housing and Urban Development (HUD.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  April 21, 2014
 11. Annual Routine Landscape Maintenance - Marguerite Parkway Slope Rehabilitation

  Council Member Schlicht announced that last year she had wanted to create a master plan
  to serve the entire community on landscape issues. She stated that she is against this
  because she believes it is an uneven distribution of tax dollars and a 15th amendment to the
  contract with West Coast Arborists is crazy.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  approve the Fifth Amendment to Contract Area 3 with Spectrum Care Landscape, Inc., to
  increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $140,000.00; and (2) approve the
  Fifteenth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc., to increase
  the contract in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

13. Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvement, Via Florecer to Trabuco
  Road (CIP 220)

  Council Member Schlicht stated that staff is concentrating on one part of town for the
  landscape and until there is a fair master plan in place and dollars are being spread evenly
  throughout the community, she will vote no on agenda items 13 and 14.

  Director Rattay noted that the reason the money is being used on Marguerite Parkway is
  because the bulk of the grant was for the removal of turf and Marguerite is approximately
  10 miles of turf and trees. He stated that it has less to do with the actual street and more to
  do with the location of the majority of turf in the City.

  City Manager Wilberg reminded the Council that the grant monies cannot be shifted to
  other areas of the City.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve
  the plans and specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction for the subject
  project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  9  April 21, 2014
 14. Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvement, Trabuco Road to Alicia Parkway
  (CIP 221)

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 14-13 Amending the Fiscal Year 2013-2014 Budget to Create Capital
  Improvement Project 221 to Construct the Marguerite Parkway Median Improvement
  Project from Trabuco Road to Alicia Parkway; and (2) approve the bid specifications and
  authorize staff to advertise for construction for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: presented a list of items related to OCFA and he wondered if
  the Council Members or the public even know what these matters are about.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

20. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

21. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

22. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

23. Orange County Vector Control District

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report.

City Council Minutes  10  April 21, 2014
 24. SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley deferred the report to the next meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

Council Member Reardon

27. Request for Moratorium on Establishment of E-Cigarette Lounges and Retail Outlets
  Within the City

  Council Member Reardon presented her report.

  James Whiting, M.V.: discussed his business, E-Cig City, which was started by his father in
  law. He noted that electronic cigarettes give people an opportunity to quit smoking and it is
  a healthier alternative to tobacco use. He further stated that in order to avoid juvenile use
  of E-Cigs, it is important for business owners and the community to regulate it.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to direct
  preparation of a GC Sec. 65858 Moratorium and process as required by law on the sale and
  the commercial use of all Electronic Cigarettes in the City of Mission Viejo.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Reardon
  NOES:  Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness to adopt a non-urgency ordinance that would
  develop land-use standards for E-Cig shops to follow but would not halt any applications
  that are in process or existing shops. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct
  staff to bring back details on the City of Laguna Niguel's action to declare E-Cigarette
  stores as specialty retail.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  11  April 21, 2014
 STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

25. Orange County Emergency Medical Services (OCEMS) Ambulance Services RFP
  Update

  City Manager Wilberg distributed a short update, including copies of letters that other
  jurisdictions have sent to the State requesting a one-year extension to the existing
  ambulance provider contracts.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed his attendance at a recent County Board of
  Supervisors meeting and the subject of advanced life support charges which ambulance
  providers are required to charge.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

26. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she and several staff members attended the 26th annual
Medal of Valor luncheon last Thursday. She stated that it is a wonderful event and Mission
Viejo resident Marilyn McDougall plans it each year. Council Member Reardon noted that she
has two copies of the Medal of Valor video and booklet that she is willing to give away so she
asked those who are interested to contact her. Council Member Reardon outlined upcoming
events including the Mission Viejo Rotary Club's annual Mayor's Prayer Breakfast on May 1 at
7:30 a.m., a National Day of Prayer event at the civic center, also on May 1, the Arts Alive
Festival on May 3 and 4, and the Wounded Warriors softball game on May 3. She also discussed
the upcoming Teen Survival Guide program which will be held on April 30 and she noted that it
is recommended for parents as well as teens. Council Member Reardon stated that Mission
Viejo has wonderful volunteers and some of them were recently honored by OneOC during their
Spirit of Volunteerism event and she commended those individuals on a job well done. Finally,
Council Member Reardon reminded residents of the Lord of the Strings concerts with Doyle
Dykes at the Dana Point Community House on Friday April 25 at 7:30 p.m. and at the Mission
Viejo Civic Center on Saturday April 26 at 7:00 p.m. (tickets are $40 each.)

City Council Minutes  12  April 21, 2014
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht noted that she is always telling people to educate themselves on the
Common Core education program and she stated that a big part of the problem is that the
curriculum was not written by teachers or educators, it's not tested or benchmarked, standards are
not rigorous and students will be two years behind. It's a one size fits all program and is not
adapted to the individual student. She recently learned that the standards are copyrighted and
mistakes have been found, but the materials cannot be corrected because of the copyright. She
encouraged everyone to attend a presentation on the subject on Saturday, April 26 from 6:30 to
8:30 p.m. at 330 W. 6th Street in Tustin. Council Member Schlicht announced that the latest
edition of the Community Common Sense newspaper is out and she encouraged everyone to get a
copy. She also stated that the biggest mistake the Council majority made tonight was to vote for
the Nadadores contract. She said that it's an incomplete contract and it won't be public until it is
signed and done. Council Member Schlicht noted that the Nadadores are an important part of the
community but the public didn't have an opportunity to be informed of the taxpayer subsidies
and to properly vet the issues. She finds the whole thing very disturbing and she stated that staff
provided misleading responses to her questions and she feels that the Council pretty much
railroaded it through, without allowing the public the opportunity to be involved like they were
15 years ago. Council Member Schlicht discussed her no vote on the Pavion Park renovation
and stated that it was a 6 year-old project that was on the shelf and it didn't go through the public
process. The cost is outrageous and the City is creating more and more regional parks that are
being subsidized by the Mission Viejo taxpayers. She noted that the City already supports a
regional dog park, animal shelter, library, community center, the Nadadores team and the
YMCA. She further discussed the City landscaping issues and stated that there is an uneven
distribution of tax dollars for renovation projects and the money is only being spent on the civic
core. Going back to the Nadadores, Council Member Schlicht said that they have a financial
responsibility and the City should have had an opportunity to see their financial records in order
to understand what their assets and liabilities are and she reminded the Council of the Nadadores'
threat to leave Mission Viejo if they don't get a $1 million dive board. Council Member Schlicht
ended her comments with a quote from Thomas Jefferson: "All tyranny needs to gain a foothold
is for people of good conscience to remain silent."

Council Member Ury

Due to the late hour, Council Member Ury passed on his comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that it was a great night last week, honoring Frank Ury as
the new President of the ACC-OC. He noted that the Murray Center looked beautiful and people
from other communities were very impressed by the facility. He also outlined his attendance at
an event in San Juan Capistrano to honor Tony Moiso. Mr. Moiso spent about 30 minutes talking
about how this community was started and he noted that the reason Mission Viejo is so great is
that "they had the courage to pull the trigger." Mayor Pro Tem Leckness stated that the new La
Paws Park is phenomenal and hundreds of dogs and their owners attended the grand opening
event and everyone was so happy. He expressed that when the Council decides to spend $1
City Council Minutes  13  April 21, 2014
 million on something, one wonders if it will work but the dog park looked great, staff was proud,
everyone was connected and they felt like the park is theirs. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
asked for prayers for Council Member Reardon who is having surgery in a couple of days.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley announced that she got home late last night after being gone for 2 weeks on family
business. She thanked her colleagues for covering the many events that took place while she was
gone and Mayor Pro Tem Leckness for chairing the last City Council Meeting. She also
announced that there will be a Red Cross blood drive at City Hall on Friday, April 25 from 12:00
to 6:00 p.m. The event is sponsored by the City of Mission Viejo in partnership with AYSO
Soccer and that partnership has increased donations significantly. Mayor Kelley encouraged
residents to call her for an appointment or sign up on the Red Cross website. She further
announced that the City will be celebrating Earth Day and Arbor Day on April 26 with volunteer
planting along Avery Parkway between Marguerite and the golf course. In conjunction, the City
will host a Green Expo event at Coronado Park on Las Ondas Drive from 8:00 a.m. to 12
noon. Also on April 26th, the City will hold a National Take-Back event where residents can
drop off old prescription medications between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. Mayor
Kelley reminded the community that Arts Alive will be held on May 3 and 4 and on May 7 there
will be a presentation for teens called The Pyramid of Success. This is a John Wooden program
that is presented by a very good speaker and while the event is free, reservations are encouraged
so she asked that people contact her to sign up.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:56 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, May 5, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 5, 2014

City Council Minutes  14  April 21, 2014
